text: A suited person walks near picture-center-right, white road markings cross the upper and lower frame, and cracked asphalt fills nearly every remaining area.
intent: This photo seems to emphasize a lone figure moving through a large geometric field.

title: Place the subject in the open gap between road markings.
why: The isolated figure at picture-center-right stays readable because asphalt surrounds him while nearby lines frame rather than cover him.

items.effect: The small figure becomes the only human focal point.

items.where: from picture-left to picture-right across the lower middle
items.effect: The road edge separates the figure from the broad foreground.
The bright diagonal adds direction without intersecting the subject.
The vertical marking balances the figure while leaving a clear gap.

summary: The road and suit are evenly lit, with little visible shadow around the feet at picture-center-right.
direction: The broad light direction cannot be determined from the frame.
cues: even asphalt brightness across the upper and lower frame
weak foot shadows below the person's shoes at picture-center-right
test: Look for cloud cover or compare the subject's feet and collar shadows before shooting.

summary: The camera is elevated above the road and aimed downward, leaving the figure small against asphalt.
viewpoint: high viewpoint with a downward tilt and no visible horizon
order: first look: the walking figure at picture-center-right
second look: the white markings entering from the frame edges

observe: Find a high overlook where the pavement fills the frame and markings create a clean gap.
decide: Put the walker in that gap with clear asphalt around the head, hands, and feet.
adjust: Change only the walker's position relative to the markings by directing the walking path slightly aside.
check: The figure remains unobstructed while at least two markings still frame the movement.

fixed: Keep the camera viewpoint, framing, light, and walking pace the same.
change: Move the subject's walking path sideways relative to the road markings.
expect: The subject shifts from the open asphalt gap toward the middle road edge in picture-center-right.
gain: A stronger graphic relationship between person and lines.
lose: Some surrounding negative space around the legs.

prep: Use an elevated roadside viewpoint on an overcast or evenly shaded day; starting point: frame the person at picture-center-right with generous asphalt around them.
a: Place the walker in the open gap between the middle and right markings.
b: Use the same framing and timing, but have the walker cross onto the middle road edge.
check: Choose the version where the head, hands, and feet remain distinct from bright markings.

items.how: Shoot downward while a person crosses between painted bays.
items.fits: Works when the floor has sparse bright lines and broad empty areas.
items.not: Does not work when parked cars cover most of the pavement.

items.how: Wait for one walker to enter a clean section between lane markings.
items.fits: Works when the street surface dominates and the person is separated from traffic.
items.not: Does not work when safety requires standing close to moving vehicles.

candidates: subject in an open gap: chosen because the visible lines frame the figure without merging with the body
high viewpoint: useful but not chosen because the exact elevation is uncertain
waiting for a walking stride: supportive but secondary to the subject's position between markings
unknowns: The exact camera height and lens choice are not visible.
The light may be overcast sky or open shade.
The person's actual walking direction and timing are not confirmed.
known: No author notes or EXIF confirm the shooting settings
